text: The domain of the function $f(x)=\sin ^{-1}\left [2x^{2}-3\right ]+\log _{2}\left (\log _{\frac{1}{2}}\left (x^{2}-5x+5\right )\right )$, where [t] is the greatest integer function, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $\sin ^{-1}[2x^{2}-3]$, the integer $[2x^{2}-3]$ must lie in $[-1,1]$, i.e. be $-1$, $0$ or $1$. This holds exactly when $-1\leq 2x^{2}-3<2$, because $[t]\leq 1$ for every $t<2$:

$2\leq 2x^{2}<5\Rightarrow 1\leq x^{2}<\dfrac{5}{2}\Rightarrow x\in \left (-\sqrt{\dfrac{5}{2}},-1\right ]\cup \left [1,\sqrt{\dfrac{5}{2}}\right )$

For $\log _{2}\left (\log _{1/2}(x^{2}-5x+5)\right )$, the inner logarithm must be positive: $\log _{1/2}(x^{2}-5x+5)>0\Rightarrow 0<x^{2}-5x+5<1$.

$x^{2}-5x+5>0\Rightarrow x<\dfrac{5-\sqrt{5}}{2}$ or $x>\dfrac{5+\sqrt{5}}{2}$.

$x^{2}-5x+4<0\Rightarrow (x-1)(x-4)<0\Rightarrow 1<x<4$.

Together: $x\in \left (1,\dfrac{5-\sqrt{5}}{2}\right )\cup \left (\dfrac{5+\sqrt{5}}{2},4\right )$, roughly $(1,1.38)\cup (3.62,4)$.

Intersecting with the first set, where $\sqrt{5/2}\approx 1.58$, leaves only $x\in \left (1,\dfrac{5-\sqrt{5}}{2}\right )$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift

text: Let S be the set of all $(α,β),π<α,β<2π$, for which the complex number $\frac{1-i\sin α}{1+2i\sin α}$ is purely imaginary and $\frac{1+i\cos β}{1-2i\cos β}$ is purely real. Let $Z_{αβ}=\sin 2α+i\cos 2β,(α,β)\in S$. Then $\sum\limits _{(α,β)\in S}\left (iZ_{αβ}+\frac{1}{i\bar{Z}_{αβ}}\right )$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\because$ $\frac{1-i\sin α}{1+2i\sin α}$ is purely imaginary

$\therefore$ $\frac{1-i\sin α}{1+2i\sin α}+\frac{1+i\sin α}{1-2i\sin α}=0$

$\Rightarrow 1-2\sin ^{2}α=0$

$\therefore$ $α=\frac{5π}{4},\frac{7π}{4}$

and $\frac{1+i\cos β}{1-2i\cos β}$ is purely real

$\frac{1+i\cos β}{1-2i\cos β}-\frac{1-i\cos β}{1+2i\cos β}=0$

$\Rightarrow \cos β=0$

$\therefore$ $β=\frac{3π}{2}$

$\therefore$ $S=\left \{\left (\frac{5π}{4},\frac{3π}{2}\right ),\left (\frac{7π}{4},\frac{3π}{2}\right )\right \}$

$Z_{αβ}=1-i$ and $Z_{αβ}=-1-i$

$\therefore$ $\sum\limits _{(α,β)\in S}\left (iZ_{αβ}+\frac{1}{iZ–_{αβ}}\right )=i(-2i)+\frac{1}{i}\left [\frac{1}{1+i}+\frac{1}{-1+i}\right ]$

$=2+\frac{1}{i}\frac{2i}{-2}=1$

text: If for $\mathrm{p}\neq \mathrm{q}\neq 0$, the function $f(x)=\frac{\sqrt{7\mathrm{p}(729+x)}-3}{\sqrt{3 729+\mathrm{q}x}-9}$ is continuous at $x=0$, then :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f(x)=\frac{\sqrt{7p(729+x)}-3}{\sqrt{3 729+qx}-9}$

for continuity at $x=0$, $\lim _{x\to 0}f(x)=f(0)$

Now, $\therefore$ $\lim _{x\to 0}f(x)=\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{\sqrt{7p(729+x)}-3}{\sqrt{3 729+qx}-9}$

$\Rightarrow p=3$ (To make indeterminate form)

So, $\lim _{x\to 0}f(x)=\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{\left (3^{7}+3x\right )^{\dfrac{1}{7}}-3}{(729+qx)^{\dfrac{1}{3}}-9}$

$=\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{3\left [\left (1+\frac{x}{3 6}\right )^{\dfrac{1}{7}}-1\right ]}{9\left [\left (1+\frac{q}{729}x\right )^{\dfrac{1}{3}}-1\right ]}=\frac{1}{3}.\frac{\frac{1}{7}.\frac{1}{3 6}}{\frac{1}{3}.\frac{q}{729}}$

$\therefore$ $f(0)=\frac{1}{7q}$

$\therefore$ Option (B) is correct.

text: The equations of the sides $\mathrm{AB},\mathrm{BC}$ and CA of a triangle ABC are $2x+y=0,x+\mathrm{p}y=39$ and $x-y=3$ respectively and $\mathrm{P}(2,3)$ is its circumcentre. Then which of the following is NOT true?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
$A$ is the intersection of $2x+y=0$ and $x-y=3$: $A(1,-2)$.

The circumcentre $P(2,3)$ lies on the perpendicular bisector of every side, so $B$ is the reflection of $A$ in the line through $P$ perpendicular to $AB$, and $C$ is the reflection of $A$ in the line through $P$ perpendicular to $AC$.

$AB$ has slope $-2$, so the perpendicular bisector of $AB$ is $y-3=\dfrac{1}{2}(x-2)$, i.e. $x-2y+4=0$. Reflecting $A$:

$\dfrac{x-1}{1}=\dfrac{y+2}{-2}=\dfrac{-2(1+4+4)}{5}=-\dfrac{18}{5}\Rightarrow B\left (-\dfrac{13}{5},\dfrac{26}{5}\right )$

$AC$ has slope 1, so the perpendicular bisector of $AC$ is $x+y=5$. Reflecting $A$:

$\dfrac{x-1}{1}=\dfrac{y+2}{1}=\dfrac{-2(1-2-5)}{2}=6\Rightarrow C(7,4)$

Slope of $BC=\dfrac{4-26/5}{7+13/5}=-\dfrac{1}{8}$, so $BC$ is $x+8y=39$ and $p=8$. Also $AC^{2}=6^{2}+6^{2}=72$.

(A) $9p=72=AC^{2}$: true. (B) $AC^{2}+p^{2}=72+64=136$: true.

$\text{Area}=\dfrac{1}{2}\left |1\left (\dfrac{26}{5}-4\right )-\dfrac{13}{5}(4+2)+7\left (-2-\dfrac{26}{5}\right )\right |=\dfrac{1}{2}\left |\dfrac{6-78-252}{5}\right |=\dfrac{162}{5}=32.4$

(C) $32<32.4<36$: true. (D) $34<32.4$ fails, so (D) is not true.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift

text:
A six faced die is biased such that

$3\times \mathrm{P}($a prime number$)~=6\times \mathrm{P}($a composite number$)~=2\times \mathrm{P}(1)$.

Let X be a random variable that counts the number of times one gets a perfect square on some throws of this die. If the die is thrown twice, then the mean of X is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let P(a prime number) = $α$

P(a composite number) = $β$

and P(1) = $γ$

$\because$ $3α=6β=2γ=k$ (say)

and $3α+2β+γ=1$

$\Rightarrow k+\frac{k}{3}+\frac{k}{2}=1\Rightarrow k=\frac{6}{11}$

Mean = np where n = 2

and p = probability of getting perfect square

$=P(1)+P(4)=\frac{k}{2}+\frac{k}{6}=\frac{4}{11}$

So, mean $=2.\qquad \left (\frac{4}{11}\right )=\frac{8}{11}$

text: Let f be a differentiable function satisfying $f(x)=\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\int\limits _{0}^{\sqrt{3}}f\left (\frac{λ^{2}x}{3}\right )\mathrm{d}λ,x>0$ and $f(1)=\sqrt{3}$. If $y=f(x)$ passes through the point $(α,6)$, then $α$ is equal to $_____________$.

solution.body:

$f^{'}(x)=\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\int\limits _{0}^{\sqrt{3}}\frac{λ^{2}}{3}f^{'}\left (\frac{λ^{2}x}{3}\right )dλ$

$\therefore$ $\sqrt{3}f^{'}(x)=\left [\frac{λ}{x}.f\left (\frac{λ^{2}x}{3}\right )\right ]_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}-\int\limits _{0}^{\sqrt{3}}\frac{1}{x}f\left (\frac{λ^{2}x}{3}\right )dx$

$xf^{'}(x)=\frac{f(x)}{2}$

On integrating we get : $\ln y=\frac{1}{2}\ln x+\ln c$

$\because$ $f(1)=\sqrt{3}$ then $c=\sqrt{3}$

$\therefore$ ($α$, 6) lies on

$\therefore$ $y=\sqrt{3x}$

$\therefore$ $6=\sqrt{3α}\Rightarrow α=12$.

text: Let $\vec{a}$, $\vec{b}$, $\vec{c}$ be three non-coplanar vectors such that $\vec{a}$ $\times$ $\vec{b}$ = 4$\vec{c}$, $\vec{b}$ $\times$ $\vec{c}$ = 9$\vec{a}$ and $\vec{c}$ $\times$ $\vec{a}$ = $α\vec{b}$, $α$ > 0. If $\left |\vec{a}\right |+\left |\vec{b}\right |+\left |\vec{c}\right |=\frac{1}{36}$, then $α$ is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given,

$\vec{a}\times \vec{b}=4.\vec{c}$ ..... (i)

$\vec{b}\times \vec{c}=9.\vec{a}$ ..... (ii)

$\vec{c}\times \vec{a}=α.\vec{b}$ .... (iii)

Taking dot products with $\vec{c},\vec{a},\vec{b}$ we get

$\vec{a}\quad .\vec{b}=\vec{b}.\vec{c}=\vec{c}.\vec{a}=0$

Hence,

(i) $\Rightarrow |\vec{a}|.|\vec{b}|=4.|\vec{c}|$ ..... (iv)

(ii) $\Rightarrow |\vec{b}|.|\vec{c}|=9.|\vec{a}|$ ..... (v)

(iii) $\Rightarrow |\vec{c}|.|\vec{a}|=α.|\vec{b}|$ .... (vi)

Multiplying (iv), (v) and (vi)

$\Rightarrow |\vec{a}|.|\vec{b}|.|\vec{c}|=36α$ ..... (vii)

Dividing (vii) by (iv) $\Rightarrow |\vec{c}|^{2}=9α\Rightarrow |\vec{c}|=3\sqrt{α}$ ..... (viii)

Dividing (vii) by (v) $\Rightarrow |\vec{a}|^{2}=4α\Rightarrow |\vec{a}|=2\sqrt{α}$

Dividing (viii) by (vi) $\Rightarrow |\vec{b}|^{2}=36\Rightarrow |\vec{b}|=6$

Now, as given, $3\sqrt{α}+2\sqrt{α}+6=\frac{1}{36}\Rightarrow \sqrt{α}=\frac{-43}{36}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Evening Shift
